question: what a stylesheet trimmed against a whole site removes by mistake, whether the trimmed pages render the same, whether a page the crawl missed is safe, and how many bytes the trim saves on a first view
instrument: Chromium CDP CSS.takeCoverageDelta and CSS.getStyleSheetText; Playwright full-page screenshots with page.route answering the trimmed text, compared pixel by pixel on a canvas; Node zlib brotli 5; src/trim buildTrimManifest and guardPage

method.pages: the pages that loaded in measurements/trim/2026-10-19.json, home first, then the internal pages in that order
method.fetch: HTML, stylesheets and scripts through the context request API with the same user agent; stylesheets and scripts are the same-origin files each page links
method.manifest: buildTrimManifest over every page, every linked same-origin script and every linked same-origin stylesheet of the site
method.oracle A: a rule is used when CDP CSS rule usage marks it used at load or after the scroll; it is a false removal when its text is not in the trimmed stylesheet
method.oracle B: three full-page screenshots per page at 1280 px width with reduced motion and animations disabled, after scrolling to the bottom in 120 ms steps and back: original, original again (the control) and trimmed; trimmed stylesheets are answered through page.route; differing pixels counted over the common area on a canvas, any channel
method.leave-one-out: per internal page, a manifest built from the other pages, their scripts and their stylesheets; the guard is run on the left-out page, and Oracle A when it does not fire
method.saved: brotli-5 of each stylesheet before and after; a page counts only the stylesheets new to the visit, home first
method.site concurrency: 3 sites at once, one context per site, 250 ms between page visits of a site
